title: Coordinate central filtration of the unitriangular group with diagonal conjugation weights
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $n\geq1$. Group schemes are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and closed immersions as in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $B_n\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] be the invertible upper triangular matrix group scheme, and let $U_n\subseteq B_n$ be its upper unitriangular subgroup. Thus $U_n(R)$ consists of matrices with diagonal entries $1$ and all entries below the diagonal zero, for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$. Put $m=n(n-1)/2$ and order the pairs $(i,j)$ with $1\leq i<j\leq n$ by increasing $j-i$, then increasing $i$; write them $C_1,\ldots,C_m$. For $0\leq r\leq m$ let $U^{(r)}\subseteq U_n$ be the closed subscheme given by $u_{ij}=0$ for $(i,j)=C_l$ with $l\leq r$. These are closed normal subgroup schemes of $B_n$, with $U^{(0)}=U_n$ and $U^{(m)}=1$. For each $1\leq r\leq m$, writing $C_r=(i_r,j_r)$, the coordinate map
$$p_r:U^{(r-1)}\longrightarrow\mathbf G_a,\qquad u\longmapsto u_{i_rj_r}$$
is a faithfully flat finitely presented group-scheme homomorphism with scheme-theoretic kernel $U^{(r)}$, and induces an isomorphism $U^{(r-1)}/U^{(r)}\simeq\mathbf G_a$. Here $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ and $\mathbf G_m(R)=R^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]; the quotient is the sheafification of $R\mapsto U^{(r-1)}(R)/U^{(r)}(R)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. For every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, every $b\in B_n(R)$ and $u\in U^{(r-1)}(R)$,
$$p_r(bub^{-1})=(b_{i_ri_r}b_{j_rj_r}^{-1})p_r(u).$$
In particular the conjugation action on this additive quotient factors through the diagonal homomorphism $B_n\to\mathbf G_m^n$ and is given by the character $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\mapsto t_{i_r}t_{j_r}^{-1}$; $U_n$ acts trivially on every quotient. When $n=1$ the filtration has length zero and $U_n=1$.

source.place: Example 6.49(a)--(c), printed pp.136--137; Theorem 16.21 proof, printed p.330, uses precisely these coordinate quotients.

proof.text:
Write $x_l=x_{C_l}$. The affine coordinate rings are
$$k[B_n]=k[d_1^{\pm1},\ldots,d_n^{\pm1},x_1,\ldots,x_m],\qquad k[U^{(r)}]=k[x_{r+1},\ldots,x_m].$$
Indeed, on upper triangular matrices the determinant expansion has only the identity-permutation term, $\prod_i d_i$: a permutation with $\sigma(i)\leq i$ for every $i$ must be the identity. A unit product in a commutative ring has each factor a unit. Thus these presentations follow by imposing the below-diagonal equations in $\operatorname{GL}_n$, then $d_i=1$, then $x_l=0$ for $l\leq r$. The resulting surjections of coordinate rings give closed immersions. The displayed rings have finitely many generators (write $d_i^{-1}$ as an additional generator with relation $d_i d_i^{-1}=1$), so the schemes are of finite type over $k$. Polynomial substitutions give all morphisms used below, by contravariance of affine spectra.

source.place: Example 6.49(a)--(c), printed pp.136--137; explicit coordinate-ring verification of the displayed filtration.

proof.text:
For a strictly upper triangular matrix $N$, the entries of $N^q$ are sums over chains of $q$ strictly increasing steps from the row to the column, so $N^n=0$. Consequently $(I+N)^{-1}=I-N+\cdots+(-N)^{n-1}$, as multiplication telescopes. If $I+N,I+M\in U^{(r)}(R)$ and $C_l=(a,b)$ with $l\leq r$, then
$$(NM)_{ab}=\sum_{a<c<b}N_{ac}M_{cb}=0,$$
since $(a,c)$ has smaller height than $(a,b)$ and is among the killed coordinates. The same chain formula makes $(N^q)_{ab}=0$ for every $q\geq1$. Thus $I+N+M+NM$ and $(I+N)^{-1}$ satisfy all the defining equations; identity does too. These are polynomial identities, valid over every commutative $k$-algebra, and define closed subgroup schemes. The empty and full equation lists give $U^{(0)}=U_n$ and $U^{(m)}=1$.

source.place: Example 6.49(a)--(c), printed pp.136--137; explicit coordinate-ring verification of the displayed filtration.

proof.text:
Let $b\in B_n(R)$. Put $D=\operatorname{diag}(b_{11},\ldots,b_{nn})$ and $b=D(I+T)$ with $T$ strictly upper triangular. The preceding finite inverse formula shows $b^{-1}$ is upper triangular with $(b^{-1})_{jj}=b_{jj}^{-1}$. For $u=I+N$,
$$(bub^{-1}-I)_{ab}=\sum_{a\leq p<q\leq b} b_{ap}N_{pq}(b^{-1})_{qb}.$$
If $C_l=(a,b)$ with $l\leq r$ and $u\in U^{(r)}(R)$, every proper subinterval $(p,q)$ has smaller height and its entry $N_{pq}$ vanishes; the remaining term has $N_{ab}=0$. Entries on and below the diagonal vanish as well. Hence conjugation by $b$ preserves $U^{(r)}(R)$; applying this also to $b^{-1}$ gives equality. This proves normality in $B_n$ for every $r$. If instead $u\in U^{(r-1)}(R)$ and $(a,b)=C_r$, exactly the proper-subinterval terms vanish, giving
$$(bub^{-1})_{i_rj_r}=b_{i_ri_r}b_{j_rj_r}^{-1}u_{i_rj_r}.$$
All formulas hold on the coordinate rings, so they also give the scheme identities.

source.place: Example 6.49(a)--(c), printed pp.136--137; explicit coordinate-ring verification of the displayed filtration.

proof.text:
Fix $1\leq r\leq m$, with $C_r=(i,j)$. For $u,v\in U^{(r-1)}(R)$, multiplication gives
$$(uv)_{ij}=u_{ij}+v_{ij}+\sum_{i<c<j}u_{ic}v_{cj}=u_{ij}+v_{ij},$$
because each $(i,c)$ has smaller height than $C_r$. Thus the polynomial coordinate map $p_r$ is a group-scheme homomorphism to $\mathbf G_a$. The section $s_r(a)=I+aE_{ij}$ belongs to $U^{(r-1)}(R)$, satisfies $p_rs_r(a)=a$, and is itself a homomorphism since $E_{ij}^2=0$. The scheme-theoretic kernel is computed on rings by
$$k[x_r,\ldots,x_m]\otimes_{k[t]}k=k[x_{r+1},\ldots,x_m],\qquad t\mapsto x_r,\quad t\mapsto0.$$
This is precisely $U^{(r)}$, including its scheme structure, by the fibre-product definition of kernel.

source.place: Example 6.49(a)--(c), printed pp.136--137; explicit coordinate-ring verification of the displayed filtration.

proof.text: Under the coordinate rings, $p_r$ is the polynomial projection associated to $k[t]\hookrightarrow k[t][x_{r+1},\ldots,x_m]$, where $t=x_r$. It is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat], with coefficient ring $B=k[t]$ and finite variable set $\{r+1,\ldots,m\}$. It is surjective because its scheme section $s_r$ supplies a preimage for every point. Thus it is faithfully flat. It is locally of finite presentation by the displayed presentation, with finitely many variables and no relations. Both source and target are affine. The target is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated], applied to its structure morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Hence $p_r$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism], and quasi-compact and quasi-separated by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Together these give finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. This includes $r=m$, when there are no remaining variables and $p_m$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), Tag 01SG (lemma-affine-permanence, part (4)), and Tag 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated); applied to the coordinate projection in Milne 6.49(b).

proof.text:
On every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the homomorphism $p_r$ induces a bijective homomorphism
$$U^{(r-1)}(R)/U^{(r)}(R)\longrightarrow (R,+).$$
Its inverse sends $a$ to the coset of $s_r(a)$: for any $u$, the element $u\,s_r(p_r(u))^{-1}$ is in the kernel, so this inverse also recovers the coset of $u$. Both maps commute with every algebra homomorphism, hence give an isomorphism of group-valued presheaves. The presheaf $R\mapsto R=\mathbf G_a(R)$ is an fppf sheaf: apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to $X=\mathbf G_a$, restricting to affine test schemes. Faithfully flat finitely presented affine coverings are fpqc coverings in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. The descended morphism remains over $k$ by uniqueness applied to the structure maps. Therefore the presheaf quotient is already this represented sheaf. Its sheafification is canonically unchanged by the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. It follows that $U^{(r-1)}/U^{(r)}\simeq\mathbf G_a$ as group sheaves, represented by this group scheme.

source.place: Tag 023Q, lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms; applied after the explicit coset calculation for Milne Example 6.49(b).

proof.text: For upper triangular matrices $(bc)_{ii}=b_{ii}c_{ii}$, so the diagonal coordinates define a homomorphism $\delta:B_n\to\mathbf G_m^n$. The conjugation identity of step 3, transported along the explicit quotient identification of step 6, is multiplication by $b_{ii}b_{jj}^{-1}$. This is exactly the character $(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\mapsto t_it_j^{-1}$ composed with $\delta$. It follows that the action factors through the diagonal; $U_n$ acts trivially since all its diagonal entries are $1$. In particular the filtration is central as a filtration of $U_n$. For $n=1$ there are no pairs, $m=0$, and the ring $k[U_n]=k$ makes the claimed length-zero filtration and $U_n=1$ explicit.
